result: Backend tests and frontend build pass. Mods UI propagates role/status, hides mutations for viewers/running servers, and provides install/update/toggle/uninstall/bulk/profile controls with confirmations/results and required profile version payload. Backend uses Portal-resolved HTTPS URLs, archive metadata, dependency checks, mutation semaphore, stopped guard, journal, rollback paths, dependent-uninstall rejection, profile persistence, and CSRF/audit/RBAC. Material gaps remain: journal recovery only deletes stale journal; bulk promotion can overwrite archives and rollback deletes overwritten destinations; SQLite/mod-list are not transactionally restored on all failures; archive metadata name/version is not safely validated before path construction; dependency validation is inconsistent; profile apply ignores required versions; no endpoint/failure-injection integration tests.

evidence.outcome: role/status guards, controls, confirmations/results, and profile version payload wired
Portal HTTPS/archive metadata, semaphore, stopped guard, journal, uninstall/profile/dependency features present
mod routes inherit authenticated CSRF/audit/admin-owner mutation authorization

next_slice.summary: Harden durable journal replay/rollback, preserve overwritten bulk archives, restore SQLite/mod-list/files together, validate archive metadata/path and dependencies consistently, honor profile required versions, and add focused failure-injection/endpoint role tests.

blockers: Bulk/normal commits do not atomically restore SQLite, mod-list, and archives on all failures.
